source_text: Sancti estote quia ego sanctus sum. Separatio a immunditia animae. Amen.
orientation: Origen is concluding his moral application of the clean and unclean creatures, quoting Leviticus' command to be holy and applying it to the soul.
pass_a_gloss: Be holy, because I am holy. Separation from the uncleanness of the soul. Amen.

choices.why: The imperative plural matches the biblical command addressed to the community; 'holy' is the fixed glossary rendering for sanctus.
The causal clause preserves the ground of the command; 'holy' follows the glossary.

choices.english: Separation from the uncleanness of the soul
choices.why: The noun phrase is kept as a terse definitional statement; 'uncleanness' renders immunditia in line with the glossary's 'unclean' for immundus.
rejected: A separation from the soul's uncleanness
Being separated from the uncleanness of the soul

choices.why: The liturgical closing is retained as a transliteration, standard for homiletic conclusions.

bible_refs.note: Sancti estote quia ego sanctus sum

pass_b_english: "Be holy, because I am holy" (Leviticus 19:2). Separation from the uncleanness of the soul. Amen.
